confirmed_fragments.statement: If the integer anchors have opposite signs, their product is an integer at most -1. Its product-plus-one being a rational square forces the product to be at least -1; thus the product is -1 and the anchors are {-1,1}. For any other tuple element x, the two anchor conditions imply 1+x and 1-x are nonnegative, so -1≤x≤1; distinctness and nonzero membership exclude the endpoints and zero.

For nonzero common neighbor x, choose rational p,q with p²=1+x and q²=1-x. Then p²+q²=2 and p≠1. Setting t=(q-1)/(p-1) is valid and finite. Substitution yields (1+t²)(p-1)+2(1+t)=0; since 1+t²≠0 over Q, the resulting p gives x=4t(1-t²)/(1+t²)². Conversely the displayed rational p,q satisfy p²+q²=2 and produce that common neighbor. The omitted conic point with p=1 gives x=0, so it does not omit any nonzero neighbor.

For {1,-1,u,-u,v,-v}, the anchor-to-element conditions are equivalent to u,v∈C, and the four cross-pair conditions are equivalent to uv∈C. The remaining opposite-pair values are 1-u²=(1+u)(1-u) and 1-v²=(1+v)(1-v), both rational squares. The stated nonzero and noncollision conditions ensure six distinct nonzero elements; u,v∈C also exclude collisions with ±1 because 2 is not a rational square.
